sections.html:
Owners here can hire an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer from a buyer who takes the house as it is. The township sits beside Reading in Berks County, and cash appeals most when the house needs work or the date is tight.

Exeter is a second class township. It had 25,466 residents in the 2020 Census and an estimated 26,069 in July 2025, making it the third largest municipality in the county after Reading and Spring Township. Owners live in 87.1 percent of its homes, so rentals are a small slice of the market. A typical owner's home is valued at $281,800, median household income is $100,083, and 93.6 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Typical monthly cost is $1,919 with a mortgage, and typical rent is $1,632.

Reiffton, Jacksonwald, Stonersville, Lorane, Neversink, Limekiln, Baumstown and Stonetown appear in addresses and on maps, but none is a separate municipality. Your tax bill and zoning come from the township.

sections.h2: Township rules that can affect a sale
sections.html:
Check the zoning code, the historic resources rules and the short-term lodging license before signing anything. The township's code is posted online, and its Building, Zoning and Engineering department publishes forms for building, plumbing, zoning and sign permits, plus a complaint form and a flood plains map.

  • Historic resources: the zoning code sorts historic properties into Classes I to IV and routes changes to them through the Planning Commission and the Board of Supervisors. Class I status requires the owner's written consent and binds heirs and later owners. After a historic resource is demolished through neglect, the township may withhold building and occupancy permits for a year.
  • Short-term lodging: a license from the Zoning Officer lets a property serve as short-term lodging, but never for more than 90 days in a calendar year. A buyer planning nightly rentals has to apply.
  • Floodplain: the flood plains map is in the township's document center, so check whether your parcel falls on it.

If your house is a listed historic resource or sits in a mapped flood area, say so early. The Exeter Friends Meeting House, the Mordecai Lincoln House, Boonecroft, Levan Farm, Mill Tract Farm, Snyder Mill and the John Bishop House are on the National Register, and the Daniel Boone Homestead is in the township, so a property near one of them may draw questions.

The last countywide reassessment in Berks County took effect for the 1994 tax year, so assessments can sit far from sale prices. The Assessment Office at 400 E. Wyomissing Avenue in Mohnton holds the records but sends no bills and collects nothing. Ask the municipal tax collector what is owed.

Annual appeal opensJune 15

A reduction requires proof that the assessment exceeds current market value, because the law presumes it correct. High taxes or trouble paying do not count. School districts and municipalities can appeal too, often to raise a value.

No age-based or special form freezes or removes property taxes for seniors. Homestead and farmstead exclusions do exist, and the school district supplies the forms.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Berks County
sections.html:
A document conveying real estate in Berks County has an $88 base fee. The Recorder of Deeds sits on the third floor of the Berks County Services Center, 633 Court Street, Reading. It refuses personal checks for transfer tax, and a Statement of Value adds one page to the fee count.

The state tax is 1 percent of the property's value, with both parties to the deed liable. The recorder sends the state share to the Department of Revenue and the local share on to the municipality or school district. Certain family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy are exempt. Call the Recorder of Deeds to learn the total rate for your price.

Under 68 Pa.C.S. section 7308, a seller does not have to investigate the property, but may not state anything known to be false or leave out a known material defect. Under section 7306, items the seller cannot know can be answered from the best information available. The form can be delivered in person, by first-class or certified mail, or by fax, and a buyer paying cash gets the same form as any other buyer.

Cash appeals to owners who want no showings, repair lists or long wait. Examples in Exeter include an estate house that needs clearing, deferred upkeep on a home held for decades, a relocation near family, or a short-term lodging license problem. Set the offer next to what a listing would net after repairs and transfer tax, then pick the route you prefer.

After you accept an offer, the title company searches the deed history and checks for unpaid taxes or liens. Ask the municipal tax collector for any balance. If a mortgage is open, get a payoff from your lender. A cash buyer has no lender to wait on, so the date depends on title work and on when you want to move.

At closing you sign the deed and the settlement papers. The deed is recorded with the Berks County Recorder of Deeds, and the recorder sends the state share of the transfer tax to the Department of Revenue. If the house is a rental, bring the lease. If it belonged to a relative who died, bring the papers that show who can sign for the estate.

Fill out the seller disclosure with care, and keep permits and receipts for repairs. A buyer who sees complete paperwork asks fewer questions, and that shortens the time to close.

faqs.q: What sets the closing date for an Exeter Township cash sale?
faqs.a: Title work and your preferred date, since no lender's schedule applies. The deed is then recorded with the Berks County Recorder of Deeds.

faqs.q: Is Exeter Township part of Reading?
faqs.a: No. Exeter Township is its own municipality in Berks County and borders St. Lawrence borough and Birdsboro. Check your tax bill, since the township, not the city, sets your zoning.

faqs.q: May I contest my Exeter assessment while the house is for sale?
faqs.a: Yes, during the June 15 to August 1 annual window or within 40 days of a change notice. You must show the assessment exceeds market value.

faqs.q: What school district covers Exeter Township?
faqs.a: Exeter Township School District, which also takes in the borough of St. Lawrence. Its buildings are Lorane, Owatin Creek and Jacksonwald elementary schools, Reiffton Elementary School, Exeter Junior High and Exeter Township Senior High.

faqs.q: Can an Exeter house be used for short-term rentals?
faqs.a: Only with a short-term lodging license from the Zoning Officer, and the code caps use at 90 days in a calendar year. A buyer should confirm the license before counting on rental income.
